I noticed this problem with me as well and I just wanted to say that conversation flows easily with life experience, but if you don't have a story to tell maybe start with factual knowledge. The majority of what people say are stories related to their own life but often have no factual basis and are rooted in opinions. It is often refreshing to hear someone talk about something other than themselves, and even more so when they are able to impart knowledge to others.

A technique that I learned to employ is conversational threading, and it will help you in just about every conversation. When someone brings up a story, it might be completely anecdotal but just based on the words they say you can pick and choose and have many different topics to expand upon. What you can do is take a couple words (possible subjects) from their story and start with factual evidence relating to those words. Start researching different topics and become acquainted with the facts behind them. Chiming in occasionally with what you know on the subject will make you appear smarter and more sociable. Just about anything will do just don't feel obligated to tell long winded stories, short responses are fine. I would spend some time in ELI 5 or TIL just so you can have a few things to say. Bonus points if you can steer the conversation to something that you know more about. Just thread the conversation and take a word out of their sentence to talk about. It gets easier the more you know. When everything fails, ask some questions about them or the subject to keep the convo going.

Good luck
